notes.title: Becoming Saint Gameplay FAQ
notes.content:
[p]Hello believers!  [/p][p]It's been two weeks since release and we first wanted to thank all of you who took the time to play the game and leave us a review, we're almost at a 100 reviews!  [/p][p]We made several Patch Notes thanks to your feedback and we wanted to answer the most frequently asked questions that we received about the gameplay, the saving options and more! So let's dive into this new FAQ focusing on gameplay![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/a659e2003865a8d94a8a423fafa1b43047e187b5.png"][/img][/p][p]The game has a tutorial for confrontation, you can open it from the "help" panel in the bottom right:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/3b73b1aa69a389ba9c733b24964dea07de7b24f9.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Any time during the battles you can open it by [b]using "ESC" button[/b] and you have the "Open the Tutorial" button in the menu, this is how it looks like:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/e44d4ad7aff1feff619efaea1ece718724958f59.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You can also open the tutorial by clicking the [b]“?” icon[/b] in the bottom right:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/68d86a6c838e5cd4ea6863c5e1cf9c7071e18eed.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/659269e75d1a538c643427b98b75c09d6df63bef.png"][/img][/p][p]The two game modes are the "easy mode" and the "hard mode".[/p][p][/p][h3]What does easy mode do?[/h3][olist][*][p]You get more food and charisma at the start, [/p][/*][*][p]You get a little advantage at each attack and parry.
[/p][/*][/olist][h3]What does hard mode do?[/h3][olist][*][p]Starting food and charisma are lower.[/p][/*][*][p]Food production is lower.[/p][/*][*][p]Bless and curse effects in battle are reduced.[/p][/*][/olist][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/9e97eea2736899e5d2404be568851d3d24d24ee8.png"][/img][/h3][p]The game saves state [b]after each finished confrontation[/b], when it shows you the resulting map. For example, if you conquered 3 towns, and quit the game, you will have a "continue" button from the start scene.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/8d6316d00a1ea40ae3c9ec8e475399aa66935038.png"][/img][/p][h3]Your saint's name has to be unique:[/h3][p]Our idea is that each name results in a saint, saved in your list. And each saint should have a unique name, so if you want to reuse it, it should be "Peter", then "Peter II", "Peter III". If you select "clear all history" when you start a game, also the list of used names and saints will be deleted.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/45e0923033f142c4cb9081a7f2a7f99afb48c0bf.png"][/img][/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/f3119550d037dd69a8ae0539c38cee60800d35c2.png"][/img][/h3][p]Go to the start scene, [b]Settings -> There is a dedicated panel on the right with a checkbox[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/39070240f98742dbf10f78ce63edd3ae7ba5e1c5.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/97ed5469ef21187e79809a6642490a6d25e4336e.png"][/img][/p][h3]Why are battles called confrontations?[/h3][p]In Becoming Saint, in order to convert a town, you have a brawl with the inhabitants: it is not a “battle” in the sense that it is a setting where both sides are trying to convince and convert the others, and no one gets killed. [/p][p]Units attack either the energy, faith or courage of others, and once this [b]goes to zero, they will run away.[/b][/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/be16701d1581ee2a9eb14bbda9999706054c40f8.png"][/img][/p][h2][/h2][h3][b]Tips for winning confrontations[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Curse at the start: try cursing enemy units that have several members right at the start of a battle for maximum damage.[/p][/*][*][p]Buff units at start: you can bless your units (up to a point) right from the start to give them some extra resilience.[/p][/*][*][p]Exploit height: try manoeuvring your throwing units by hand and placing them on higher grounds, far from other units, for maximum advantage.[/p][/*][*][p]Conquer contiguous towns: the cost of travelling is determined from your closest controlled town, so if you go by contiguous towns, the cost in food of marching will be lower.[/p][/*][*][p]Foresee food expenses: When turning believers into followers, try checking the food computation feedback panel for its projects for the future to check whether you can afford them.[/p][/*][/list][p]You can also check our dedicated guide here:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3520997216"][/dynamiclink][/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/fa1707c724d6735d0fb55e15dcf9dd5cfbf6c96d.png"][/img][/h3][p]Units that are followers of yours and have "survived" the last battle will [b]level up every 3 towns conquered.[/b] So level up will happen when controlling 3 towns, 6, 9, 12 etc... Units level up after you get to make your speech in the Piazza here:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/ad0809363181005de681d783cc2fb3e1a83ea9e8.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]How not to die when losing confrontations?[/h3][p]You can lose a confrontation and not lose the game if:[/p][olist][*][p]Your charisma is above zero, AND[/p][/*][*][p]You did not bring all your units with you to the confrontation. [/p][/*][/olist][p]If you notice during a “battle” that you are losing it, you can always run away:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/469758ae98b49da3af0980265d0c006286d5acfe.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/283962c9f12b4ff714a5ece441e72b5e0ff57630.png"][/img][/p][p]Having units on elevation [b]always gives an advantage[/b], both in attack and in defence. Ranged units attack in two ways: if the enemy is far, they throw at it; if the enemy is in contact, they attack as all other units do. They try to attack someone all the time; the only moment they don't attack or move is when there is no one in range and no path to reach an enemy. Notice that if you select a ranged unit, its [b]range will be shown on the grid.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/e2087ea8bcb475d7c4e47e48c1b458ee822f3f01.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/e355e4a84a741ad0a86e9f3a45ffc447ee477c11.png"][/img][/p][p]“Critical” refers to "making a critical attack", if unit A is critical vs unit B, once per battle, A will attempt a "critical attack" against B (if they are fighting), which, if successful, will completely disband unit B. It is not related to or affecting normal attack results. Notice how the full unit panel shows against who the selected unit is critical:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/70ebf90f14db45ff6bd56e0e99e5229713b94599.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/79fdc5a4fc41f138c71a7972751c2a11e887a724.png"][/img][/p][h3]How to see complete infos of the current set of units, yours and the towns’?[/h3][p]Just open the full unit info panel, you can do that in Piazza, when selecting units for the march:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/eb20cc9fedcc982bbae6a36b708f84a698c4229f.png"][/img][/p][p]And also from the map, just click on the unit icon:
[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/2840a28151a42bd35e9a4eb5b89baee9c798c593.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/70ebf90f14db45ff6bd56e0e99e5229713b94599.png"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]Notice that by selecting any unit in the panel sides, its full info panel will open, so you can navigate the full roster.[/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/35d8243fe186a5f789315077d2ef5d7bf56528ec.png"][/img][/h3][p]What a choice does is revealed completely [b]once you replay a game[/b]. For every choice that you have taken previously, a large tooltip appears on the choices showing its effect: [/p][p]It is meant as a progressive discovery of content.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/ba09eceaaec68294fbeb22ea3eeb7d8e3381735e.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/be6425650b2fe1950b25c92c6ca01a469ce15c64.png"][/img][/p][h3]Where is the politics’ bless, curse, and trance effect evaluation?[/h3][p]When you are selecting units for a march there is a hint’s section, that if you close it, it remains closed. [b]Click on the bottom left to reopen it,[/b] also notice that the information on bless, curse, and trance effects is always visible.[/p][p] [/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/94282510a2b184c0c8cc51fc4d88c1268a86e28b.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/677ce14fa1ec8a0a79d0b60d777e28c5d50b1f4e.png"][/img][/carousel][h2][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/fdcc542e412705149e082d311efbafa01b5d7cc4.png"][/img][/h2][p]In order to “win” the game you need to control at least [b]13 cardinals and the town of Rome[/b], in no particular order. Here by winning it is intended miniming the time between your death and becoming a saint, which in this case would mean becoming saint while still alive 😝

[b]SPOILER: "Death down the ravine" achievement. How do you get this ending??[/b]

[spoiler] Try changing your politics frequently... [/spoiler]

[b]SPOILER How to get more food production?[/b]

[spoiler] Distributing land to people and peasants will definitely increase your food production. Also, letting merchants do their redistribution work. [/spoiler] 

That's it for our most asked questions regarding the gameplay of Becoming Saint, if you still have questions, feel free to ask us either in the Steam Discussions or on Discord!

Stay blessed!

- The Becoming Saint team -

notes.title: Dev Blog #6 - Threats and Enemies in Becoming Saint and new playtest!
notes.content:
Hey Heretics,

Our new dev blog this time will shed some light on [b]the threats[/b] we face during this journey! From food management, rebellious followers to other powers in place, fights are made on and off the battlefield.

[b][h3]Food or foe?[/h3][/b]
There are several threats to your progression in Becoming Saint: 
[list]
[*] Losing followers who run away or get converted during confrontations
[*] Not having enough food to feed your followers
[/list]
The more your conquest progresses, the more the game may set you in a dilemma, between choices that keep your policy “pure” and constant (and hence those who follow you will keep doing so) and the need for compromise to facilitate getting resources like food or charisma.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/4dbb89c499a909f3334cd1f2e4d5eaf07020cc4b.png[/img]
[i]Art made by Vic Macioci for Becoming Saint[/i]

[b]Charisma and food[/b] are the main resources and needs of your movement. Your actions change them continuously, and they are also resources that you may use to obtain new items, units, and convert one resource into another. You will need to always [b]keep charisma above zero[/b], as that is the basic element that keeps your movement together. Not having food for your units, or pursuing a contradictory policy, will harm your charisma, and hence lead to an early end of your movement and, by extension, of your… life.

However, you are not the only one who has great designs. Other forces already have a claim on Italy, and they will not let go of it easily. The forces that oppose you are of three kinds: 
[list]
[*] The Pope
[*] The Emperor
[*] The merchants and banks
[/list]
Each of these may be supported by different segments of the population, and for each town, different and partially generative collectives.
For example, the Pope has [i]bintegralist bachelors, perplex peasants and priests[/i] as default available units, plus say special ones like [i]penitent puritan women, or blind superstitious men[/i]. The Emperor has [i]cavaliers and town guards[/i], the Merchants have [i]mercenaries and wool workers[/i].
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/cc456368ccf7cafb5c2489f9d45f333910732467.png[/img]
The Pope and the Emperor were the main political powers in 14th-century Italy, together with the emerging power of the communes. These three powers were in constant conflict with each other, sometimes an openly armed one. And they all used different religious orientations to affirm their political aims. Does this mean they will oppose you completely in your movement? Not necessarily.

Depending on who you decide to conquer, your set of rules, and also your reactions in the case of “special events” (like [spoiler]the death of the Pope[/spoiler]), you will be seen as friend or enemy, and in all cases, things may change any time depending which towns you are converting. In Becoming Saint, you are creating a new political force, so in the long run, the existing main powers, Church, Empire and Merchant/banks see you as an enemy that must be destroyed, but that does not mean you can't make the most of your brief alliances with some of them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/642c688123ae2986abb041b4f6a07dfdbc685eab.gif[/img]

Your followers may see you as a leader (even as in a cult), or as a (temporary) representative of the ideas that you bring forward. All this depends on the choices you make when building your set of rules (regula), that you may also alter in time. Depending on how much your policy changes, your followers may even end up seeing you as a traitor of the movement, and that will not end well for you…
I tried to avoid setting yourself as necessarily a heroine; you may adopt a policy that is somehow more participative.

Attacks in Becoming Saint are symmetrically aimed at converting and discouraging enemies (nobody gets killed in confrontations), so they are aimed at [b]reducing belief and determination[/b], acting on the three dimensions of [b]energy, faith, and courage[/b]. To reduce these, some units curse, some throw books, some sing off-key songs, some juggle to distract, some give “gentle” slaps, and so on, and the player can also directly throw items like money on the battlefield to distract enemy units.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/72278bef9268ec4a23898a84ea575ae0e7e4e019.gif[/img]

[b][h3]New playtest starts on Friday[/h3][/b]
Our brand new playtest will start on this Friday, May 2nd, and will grant access to 500 players maximum to have a taste of all the new additions we implemented, thanks to your previous feedback.

To request access to this playtest, click on the button of the game's store page on Steam.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/69f98ebb49b7db4131de27bb38d4ba56da1b059a.png[/img]
This playtest will only last a week and you can share any feedback either on the gameplay, visuals and new additions on Discord or in the Steam discussions. Thank you for your support and help in making Becoming Saint the best experience possible!

Here is the list of the new features you can expect in this new playtest:
[list]
[*] Cardinals and new victory conditions.
[*] Complete victory conditions are now clearer, as you have to control most of the cardinals to become Popesse in your lifetime and hence a saint while alive
[*] The fact that the cardinal seat locations are mostly generative creates a greater variety of paths in the map, as you “chase” the towns with seats
[*] Units are controlled by hand by default, plus a global switch at start, and the choice is persisted.
[*] New character and feature: the illusionist, which enables new unit types.
[*] There is a slimmed-down and interactive tutorial that introduces some actions in confrontations.
[*] New handling of pauses in confrontation and sync of infos.
[/list]
[i]Thanks @Turtler on Discord for somehow giving us the source of the idea[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/af1c1f2928fcadee4a904cc48c5da913f6e33792.png[/img]

Want to learn more about the context and design ideas for Becoming Saint? Check out [url=https://peterpunk.substack.com/p/summoning-rebels-with-historical?source=queue]our post on historically inspired games here[/url].

Stay blessed, heretics!

- The Becoming Saint team -
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/Firesquid][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/f5587fa419d5105228d86f0544713ccd52f041fe.png[/img][/url][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2643010/Becoming_Saint/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/b179de58911c3ae80270f461b7fb392936338a70.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Join our open playtest on Steam!
notes.content:
Hello Heretics!

Our second playtest is now fully open [b]until March 31st[/b]! The first playtest we had was an amazing experience and your feedback helped us so much improve the game that we decided to host another one, public this time!

To participate, go to the Steam Store Page of the game and click on this button:

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2643010/Becoming_Saint/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/69f98ebb49b7db4131de27bb38d4ba56da1b059a.png[/img][/url]

From the previous closed playtest's feedback we added:
[list]
[*] Random events triggering during the march and where your choices will influence your charisma and how your followers perceive you as a good leader (or not!)
[*] Improvement of the tutorial and better gameplay explanation through tooltips
[*] More town customized for a complete immersion into medieval Italy
[*] Improvements of units controls that are now more reactive during combat phase
[*] A new icon to let you know how many cities you have converted (next to the food and charisma ressources)
[*] ...And more for you to discover in-game!
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/0b47508ab99415d08f31f2ab2fcb9077a0680f72.gif[/img]

You can share your feedback in the [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfCtSB9malT1mrv7y9BaOAwqmEIz9Gl9LdHLfSRHYB1MId-EQ/viewform]feedback form[/url] and it's also important to complete it as [b]if you want your name to appear in the contributors section of the game, it can only be gathered through this feedback report.[/b]

For specific bugs/suggestions, you can share them on our [url=https://discord.gg/6Fdxg9qR]Discord[/url] in the #feedback-march-playtest channel (and come chat with us!). All feedback is welcome and will help us shape the game to be the best experience possible!

The playtest is also [b]available on Steamdeck[/b], you can use on Discord the [b]Steamdeck[/b] tag to report anything related to the Steamdeck version.

Do not hesitate to ask us anything about the playtest or the game and we can't wait for you to begin your journey towards sanctity!

Stay blessed, heretics!

- The Becoming Saint team -

notes.title: Dev Blog #3 - Towns and Setting in Becoming Saint
notes.content:
Heretics,

Our third dev blog will preach the importance of the setting of the game and how it shapes your journey in sanctity as well as the way to achieve it through conquest.

[h3]Medieval Italy as a place of changes and evolution[/h3]

14th century Italy was an interesting place: commerce and investments were flourishing in Italy. It was the time of the birth of international banks Italy-based, but with European (and beyond) wide markets, when, at the same time, there was an emergence of pauperistic movements. These movements conflated[b] social justice and religious issues[/b], the latter part and its contrasts are masterly presented in [i]The Name Of The Rose[/i] book.
We wanted to have a setting that triggered reflection on social issues that are actually relevant for everyone today within a historical context.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/18a70bf2b07805eaac485e929c88710d72cb7bff.png[/img]
[h3]Your surroundings during battles[/h3]

At each starting game, patterns are generated for each town; platforms, fountains, and monuments are placed in the town grids accordingly to these patterns. Thanks to this mechanic, each campaign generates a different set of town grids. 
[list]
[*] Platforms give the occupying unit an advantage in both defence and attack;
[*] Fountains block a cell so that nobody can cross it;
[*] Monuments both block the cell where they are set and also can block projectiles.
[/list]
So, placing and moving units on platforms and behind fountains or monuments can be a great way to improve your chances of converting a town to your faith.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/751e528b9d1c77fa8b8cfbcca2cb431b54566ecf.gif[/img]

[h3]Giving birth to an environment[/h3]

The artistic style is directly inspired by the preference for[b] simplicity and lyricism[/b] found in the paintings of [i]Giotto[/i] and his school and by the austere and minimalist style characteristic of medieval miniatures. Consequently, the emphasis is on [b]symbolic and expressionistic[/b] value rather than on realistic and verisimilar representation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/cfab95191637d90b91b169d9503e5adb3a7f2579.png[/img]
[i]Source: Sailko, CC BY 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons & Codex Manesse, UB Heidelberg, Cod. Pal. germ. 848, fol. 14v, Markgraf Heinrich von Meißen[/i]

For the scenarios and architectural elements, let's consider for example the "2D" representations that we find in ancient manuscripts and in Giotto's paintings where architecture is predominant.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/af6d66da1d92d40a4d8260fb76f843de8d845c74.png[/img]
[i]Source: Cacciata dei diavoli da Arezzo, https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cacciata_dei_diavoli_da_Arezzo (2024, October 4), Wikipedia [/i]

We chose cities and regions that had somehow evolved at the time as independent entities, which is, of course, a new historical feature that emerged at the time. So the map of Italy is “distorted” if compared to modern projections because most “free towns” were around central Italy, so that part of Italy is wider, and as the south of Italy at the time had very few independent towns, it is shrunk. Also, in several maps of the time, [b]the upper part of the map is not north but East[/b], and that fit the user interface orientation of the game, so we adopted it

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/8540f3d46e1a697ae1104850937a5c3e92eeac05.png[/img]
[i]Source: Sailko, CC BY 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons[/i]

To you, which Italian towns are the most iconic and should have their own battle map and buildings? Feel free to comment your suggestions on Steam or share it on our [url=https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J]Discord[/url]!

The next dev blog will dive deeper into the gameplay mechanics and is planned for next month!

Stay blessed, heretics!

- The Becoming Saint team -

notes.title: A new faith has arrived: discover our game Becoming Saint! 😇
notes.content:
[h3][b]WATCH OUR ANNOUNCEMENT TEASER TRAILER[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=d7cXR6pvUvc;full][/previewyoutube]
We’re proud to introduce you to Becoming Saint, developed by OpenLab and published by Firesquid!

[h3]Storyline and Narrative[/h3]

Play as a young woman from Assisi, in medieval Italy, setting out to become a [b]preacher[/b]. You start with a small following and will pick from the vast array of [b]heretical beliefs[/b] of the time to define your creed and [b]try to convert one small town at a time[/b].

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]

The game loops around [b]conversion battles[/b] where you can pick a fitting set of units required, deploy them within the chosen town, and then the confrontation begins! You can change units’ actions to reach your goal and turn the non-heretics into your cause.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45110870/6ffdab465a49f5d0b4d85dd4cb309e4bef98327e.png[/img]
Adding counties to your domain will grow your power, resources, and influence, you can then pick in a [b]wider spectrum of behavior and political choices[/b], eventually changing previous choices that influence your evolution, leading to greater power and personal triumphs… as well as setbacks.

Join our followers and be part of our community of believers:
► [url=https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J]Discord[/url]
► [url=https://x.com/Becoming_Saint]Twitter[/url]

And support the game development by adding Becoming Saint to your wishlist: 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2643010/Becoming_Saint/

Stay tuned believers, we will soon come to you with news and holy content!

- The Becoming Saint Team -
